purpose: Desloratadine is used to relieve allergy symptoms like sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives. It helps with both seasonal allergies (like hay fever) and year-round allergies. It can also help reduce the itching and swelling from chronic hives.
how_it_works: Your body releases a chemical called histamine when it reacts to something you are allergic to, and that is what causes your allergy symptoms. Desloratadine works by blocking the histamine receptors in your body so histamine cannot trigger those uncomfortable symptoms. Unlike older antihistamines, it is much less likely to make you feel drowsy because it does not easily cross into your brain.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medicine very well. The most common side effects include headache, dry mouth, feeling tired, and an upset stomach or nausea. Some people may feel slightly drowsy, though this is less common than with older allergy medicines.
warnings: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine as it may increase drowsiness. Tell your healthcare provider about all other medicines you take to avoid interactions. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or trying to become pregnant, check with your doctor before using this medicine. Stop taking it and seek help right away if you develop a rash, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face or throat.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one 5 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. For children, the dose is lower and depends on their age and weight, so always follow your doctor or pharmacist's instructions. Try to take it at the same time each day, and you can take it any time that works best for your routine.
